72	## 5. Decisions
73	
74	### Decision D1
75	- Basis: R1, R2
76	- Minimal option: ordenar os change sets por data do commit
77	- Selected option: ordem topológica das histórias das cabeças (`git rev-list --topo-order -n 1`)
78	- Rationale: commits do mesmo segundo (comuns em lotes e testes) empatam por data; a ordem topológica lista um descendente antes dos seus ancestrais e não depende de relógio
79	- Consequences: se as cabeças divergem (nenhuma descende de todas) vale a primeira da ordem topológica, uma cabeça entre as mais novas
80	- Falsifier: um escopo de vários change sets cujo sujeito tem uma cabeça de que outra cabeça descende
81

A prova de ponta a ponta é a revisão delegada de um roadmap sem congelamento manual da ordem dos commits dos membros.

1957	func reviewBundlePayloadDigest(payload ReviewBundlePayload) (string, error) {
1958		canonical := payload
1959		// Change-set IDs and Git refs remain exported for audit/debugging but are
1960		// advisory provenance. Stable subject identity is the classified patch and
1961		// tree manifest, so provider ref movement or a derived-only follow-up commit
1962		// cannot change the bundle identity.
1963		canonical.Subject.ChangeSets = nil
1964		canonical.Subject.Base = ""
1965		canonical.Subject.Head = ""
1966		// The observation is derived from the head just cleared above, so sealing
1967		// it would smuggle that ref back into the identity: a provider ref moving,
1968		// or a derived-only follow-up commit, would flip a result from observed to
1969		// carried-forward and stale a review of content that did not move. It stays
1970		// in the written bundle for the reader, as advisory provenance, exactly
1971		// like the refs it is computed from.
1972		//
1973		// Copied first: `canonical := payload` shares the slice backing array, so
1974		// clearing in place would erase the state on the bundle the caller is
1975		// holding, not on the copy being hashed.
1976		canonical.Evidence = append([]ReviewBundleEvidence{}, canonical.Evidence...)
1977		for i := range canonical.Evidence {
1978			canonical.Evidence[i].SubjectObservation = ""
1979		}

**decision: approved**

I approved the change with four low-severity findings, all proposed as follow-ups. One problem with the draft: I couldn't run the `pose` command in this session (it was denied), so the required `artifact-check` tool has no run behind it. I marked it `not-used` and explained why. POSE's rule (g) will probably refuse the whole draft because of that, so `pose artifact-check --spec pose-review-subject-head-is-the-newest --strict` needs to be run before the draft can be recorded. I didn't run the tests myself either. Every criterion below relies on the sealed evidence plus my own reading of the code.

## What I checked

- **The fix is correct.** `git rev-list --topo-order -n 1 <heads>` returns a head that no other head descends from. In the commits it walks, only the given heads can have no child, and topo order prints those first. So when the heads are in one line of history, it picks the newest. It doesn't depend on commit dates, and the order of the sets doesn't matter. The sealed `review-subject-head-integration` check tests three orders, a single head and an unknown head.
- **Sealed bundles keep their recorded head.** `reviewBundlePayloadDigest` clears `Subject.Head` before hashing (`review_bundle.go:1965`), so the bundle's id doesn't change. `sealReviewBundle` hands back the bundle already on disk (`review_bundle.go:2100-2103` and `2143-2147`).
- **Nothing else relied on the old head.** I checked every reader of `Subject.Head`: `delegation_handoff.go:312`, `review_run_continuity.go:390`, `review_run_provenance.go:755`, `review_dispatch.go:543/1165/1534` and `review_rounds.go:592`. They read the bundle as stored, so runs already in progress still match their `SealedCommit`.
- **Spec scopes are unchanged.** With fewer than two distinct heads the function returns `""` and the old assignment stays.

- **F1** (`pose-mcp/internal/pose/review_bundle.go:4482`): `newestResolvedHead` passes the `ResolvedHead` values to `git rev-list` without checking that they're 40-character hashes and without a closing `--`. The other `rev-list` calls in this file do end with `--`. A malformed head from the index could be read as an option or a path. Only the output is checked.
- **F2** (`pose-mcp/internal/pose/review_bundle.go:783`): when the heads diverge, for example member branches joined by merge commits, one branch tip is picked silently.
